plain.text: The famine was still severe. When the grain ran out, Jacob told his sons to go back. Judah reminded him that the man had said they would not see his face unless their brother came. Judah said, "Send the boy with me. I myself will guarantee his safety; you can hold me personally responsible." Finally Israel agreed. He told them to take gifts of balm, honey, spices and nuts, and double the silver. "May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved."

When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he had his steward bring them to his house for a meal. They were afraid, thinking it was about the silver. They explained to the steward, who said, "It's all right. Don't be afraid. Your God has given you treasure in your sacks; I received your silver." He brought Simeon out to them. When Joseph came, they bowed down and gave him their gifts. He asked about their father. When he saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, he was deeply moved and hurried out to find a place to weep. Then he washed his face and came back. The brothers were seated in order of age, to their astonishment. Benjamin's portion was five times larger than anyone else's. They feasted and drank freely with him.

summary.bigIdea: Judah takes responsibility for Benjamin, and Joseph, overwhelmed with emotion, hosts his brothers at a feast.
points: Judah offers himself as a guarantee for Benjamin's safety.
Joseph weeps privately when he sees his brother Benjamin.
The brothers are seated in order of age and feast with Joseph.
summary.reflection: Judah, who once sold Joseph, now takes responsibility for Benjamin. How have you seen people change for the better?
